A novel / 02 / 2024

Cities Without Shadows

Seven cities. One sun. No place left to hide.

An expedition into seven sunlit cities, and the quiet rebellion of people learning to make darkness.

FormatNovel / 312 imagined pages
TerritoryLight, freedom, belonging
StatusFictional portfolio work
Read the opening↗
01 / The story

For ninety years, the sun has refused to set. Across seven cities, sleep is a civic duty, silence is a controlled substance, and darkness is only a word in old books. Lio, an apprentice glassmaker, discovers a material that casts a shadow. What begins as a workshop experiment becomes a question no government can answer: what is a life without a private place?

“Seven cities. One sun. No place left to hide.”
Mara Vey
Volume 02
02 / Opening passage
Original concept text

Chapter one.
A private darkness

The first shadow was the size of a button. Lio nearly swept it off the workbench with the glass dust.

It lay beneath the new piece, a small dark circle that moved when he moved the glass. He bent close. For the first time in his life, there was a place the sun could not reach.

Outside, the noon bells rang for the fourth time that day. The city had long ago learned that time was something you made together, not something the sky could be trusted to provide.

End of sample
